rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> 2-year split-plot field experiment (2004<U+2013>2005) at OSU Lewis-Brown farm with sprinkler, microspray and drip at 50/100/150% ETc on 'Duke' blueberry. Q2: Abstract and Table 4 <U+2013> drip plants had about half the shoot and root dry weight, lower root vigor (1.8 vs 3.0<U+2013>3.1) and higher Phytophthora cinnamomi root infection (14.3% vs 6.7<U+2013>7.3%) than sprinkler/microspray; authors conclude drip maintained higher soil water near plant base, creating conditions favourable to root rot. Q3: Table 4 and Results <U+2013> disease established both by plating root segments on selective media (P5ARP+H) and independently by visual root rot symptoms (premature red/yellow leaves, stunted shoots, July 2005) and root system vigor ratings at destructive harvest, with canopy cover from multispectral imaging (Fig. 2) showing the same pattern. Q4: Table 2 and Fig. 1 <U+2013> volumetric soil water content measured by TDR was 5<U+2013>6% higher under drip in 2005 (32.7% vs 27<U+2013>28%) and soil often exceeded field capacity under drip at 100<U+2013>150% ETc; Fig. 3 shows infection increased with water applied; Fig. 4B links infection to root vigor. Q7: Results/Discussion and Summary <U+2013> authors state drip increased root rot because it kept higher soil water content/matric potential in the root zone; effect tied to over-application of water (infection rose from 50% to 150% ETc) and sites with heavy soil, poor drainage or disease history are stated as less suited to drip.
rows.notes: Q3 marked yes with some doubt: plating and visual symptom/vigor rating are distinct methods on disease occurrence, though both from the same destructive sampling. Q5/Q6: single site, one silty clay loam, one cultivar, plot scale only. Q8: authors note inoculum source uncertain and that soil/water tests may have missed small amounts, and call for further study of drip lateral placement/frequency, but do not state limitations of the drip-root rot result itself. Q9: only letter groupings (P=0.05) and regression R<U+00B2> reported; no SD/SE/CI given in text.
